name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,563

clue.text: New name used by oil supplier to show good intentions

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the following word is rebuilt in a fresh letter order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
oil is drawn up from a well

explanation.surface: A company quietly rebrands itself in the oil business to look like a well-intentioned outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean well is the idiom for having kind aims even when the result falls short.

clue.text: Resin in forest fruit, principally in chestnuts

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, read here as taking the principal or leading letter of each following word

blocks.note: mast is the nuts of forest trees such as beech and oak, fallen on the woodland floor
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A sticky resin is found in woodland nuts, especially chestnuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a gum exuded by a Mediterranean tree, used in varnish and as a chewing gum.

clue.text: Coat hung up by setter without another garment

indicators.note: in a down clue, hanging something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
the setter refers to themself as I
sole means alone, with nobody else

explanation.surface: The setter hangs up a coat and stands there without another layer on.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's light sleeveless undergarment for the upper body.

clue.text: God with deep cut over sides of nose

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two outermost letters, first and last
the cut is laid over the next piece, stretching across and enclosing it

blocks.note: a gash is a long deep wound
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A deity bears a deep scar that runs over both sides of his nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganesh, the elephant-headed Hindu deity, is fittingly all about the nose: his trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganesh is the Hindu elephant-headed deity of wisdom and new beginnings, son of Shiva.

clue.text: Parent exchanged boring tool

indicators.note: the letters are swapped around with one another, giving a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A mother or father swaps one dull implement for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but here it means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepan is a surgeon's cylindrical saw for cutting holes in the skull, or a mining borer.

clue.text: Rear of bowsprit attached to crude vessel

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
crude and rough both mean unrefined

explanation.surface: The back end of a ship's bowsprit is fixed to a roughly built boat.
explanation.walkthrough: With bowsprit in the clue, 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is an open container, a long narrow vessel for animals' food or water.

clue.text: Bra recycled into little lad's garment

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and made into something new, so the letters are remade
one piece goes into the other, which surrounds it

blocks.note: a tad is a small child, a little boy
taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An old bra is made over into a little boy's top.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, once worn over armour and now as a uniform or a herald's coat.

clue.text: Good editor raised money

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
a cent is a coin, a small unit of money

explanation.surface: A worthy newspaper editor has managed to raise funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised money' looks like fundraising, but 'raised' only applies to the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent and good are synonyms meaning respectable, honest or of acceptable quality.

clue.text: Aggressive call by second in line upset regent

indicators.note: the second in a word is the letter standing in second place
upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: to give someone a bell is British slang for a phone call
the second letter of the word
taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An heir, second in line to the throne, angrily demands the regent stand aside.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, giving someone a bell means phoning them.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerent means hostile and ready to fight, a close synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Good French tenor's headgear

blocks.note: bonne is the feminine of the French word for good
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A fine French singer shows off a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a hat tied under the chin, worn by women and babies.

clue.text: Proof of English navy hacking innovative device

indicators.note: hacking cuts its way into something, so one piece breaks into the middle of the other
innovative means newly devised, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
N is the abbreviation for navy
taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Evidence that the English navy has been hacking a clever new gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is the facts or testimony that establish whether something is true, as in a court case.

clue.text: S-shaped curve over letter

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
gee is the spelt-out name of the letter G

explanation.surface: A curved stroke drawn over a letter, like an accent mark.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled from one end; scorecards abbreviate it to O.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogee is a moulding or arch with a double curve, concave and convex like an S.

clue.text: Instrument next to piece of glass containing hard protective covering

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a cello is a bowed string instrument
a pane is a sheet of window glass
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A cello stands beside a glass case with a tough protective shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellophane is a thin transparent film used for wrapping and protecting goods.

clue.text: Slob, we agree, adjusted to hard work

indicators.note: adjusted means altered and set differently, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: We all agree the lazy slob has been made to knuckle down.
explanation.walkthrough: Elbow grease is the informal idiom for vigorous physical effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow grease is a jokey name for hard physical effort, such as scrubbing or polishing.

clue.text: Tree that's almost mature associated with Christian festival

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: mature and old both mean well advanced in age
Easter celebrates the resurrection of Christ

explanation.surface: An ageing tree is linked to Easter, perhaps through palm branches.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster is a small Mediterranean tree, the wild olive or Russian olive.

clue.text: Identical edges of leaf found in seed

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters
found in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: sesame is a well-known seed
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Matching leaf margins turn up inside a seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfsame is an emphatic way of saying the very same, exactly identical.

clue.text: Herb with black fruit shedding end of skin

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
shedding means casting off, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an orange is a citrus fruit
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A herb goes with a dark fruit that has lost the tip of its peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a blue-flowered plant whose cucumber-flavoured leaves are used in salads and drinks.

clue.text: Revolt by male leaving relative small following

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word
following means coming after, so this piece is placed after the first

blocks.note: mum is a mother, a close relative
M is the abbreviation for male
tiny and small are synonyms

explanation.surface: A man walks out on a minor relation in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is an open rebellion against authority, especially by sailors against their officers.

clue.text: Red tops adapted to accommodate supportive garment for balletic figure

indicators.note: adapted means modified into a different form, so the letters are rearranged
to accommodate is to take in and house, so the other piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange; red tops are British tabloid newspapers
a bra supports the bust

explanation.surface: Tabloids have been reworked to cover a supportive garment worn by a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: Red tops are British tabloid papers, named for their red mastheads.
explanation.definitionFit: Port de bras is the ballet term for the carriage and movement of the arms.

clue.text: Child carrying most of wild old fruit

indicators.note: most of means not all, so the final letter is cut away
carrying means holding, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
wild and mad both mean crazy or frenzied
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A toddler is carrying most of a wild, ancient fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomato is botanically a fruit, though usually eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Plays for time in part of theatre

blocks.note: first meaning: delays or holds off to gain time
second meaning: the seats on the ground floor of a theatre

explanation.surface: An actor drags things out in one section of the auditorium.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means delays evasively as a verb, and as a noun the ground-floor seating of a British theatre.

clue.text: Praise for leaders of liberalism abolished under democrats

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: the first letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Political commentary praising the end of liberalism under a Democratic government.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is a formal synonym for extolling or speaking highly of someone.

clue.text: Standard source of salt found in average cheese

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter
found in means sitting inside, so that letter goes within the next word

blocks.note: par is the standard or normal level
the mean is a kind of average
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Salt is a standard ingredient of an ordinary cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard, salty Italian cheese, often grated over pasta.

clue.text: Go for a small sheet of canvas

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small
a sail is a sheet of canvas on a boat

explanation.surface: Choosing a little piece of canvas, perhaps for painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for someone is an idiom meaning to attack them, as does assail.

clue.text: Dish made from bent reeds

indicators.note: made from says the answer is formed out of the very letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, dropping the outer ones

explanation.surface: A meal woven out of bent reeds, like a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a course of a meal: the main course in America, a starter in Britain.

clue.text: Moist like a shellfish?

blocks.note: first meaning: damp and sticky
second, playful meaning: resembling a clam, adding the adjective ending to the mollusc

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey second sense, an invented adjective from the name of a bivalve.
explanation.definitionFit: Clammy describes skin or air that is unpleasantly damp and cold, like the feel of a mollusc.
